<!-- pr-reviewer: b94e29016d5af0c6890856f404c98053208b69ab -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** I found no blocker.

**What looks good**
- The fix is one line: `quat_mul(q, turn)` at `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs:271`. `quat_mul(r, q)` applies `q` first, then `r` (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/mod.rs:115`). So the turn is applied in the setup frame, then the setup orientation is applied. This is a rotation about the setup's own axes. I checked it by hand for X, Y and Z, in both directions.
- The new test `quarter_turns_follow_each_oblique_setup_axis_in_both_directions` (`wcs_page_tests.rs:204`) does not copy the fix. It writes the expected rotation of each basis vector by hand (`Rx`, `Ry`, `Rz`) and maps it to world with the frame from before the turn. I checked the three formulas against the standard rotation matrices: they are correct. The test uses an oblique frame (23, -31, 47 degrees), so a world-frame turn fails it. The test also checks that the origin does not move.
- Command path is unchanged: `turn_wcs` queues `CommandKind::SetWcs`. `dispatch_set_wcs` (`crates/ui/src/state_wcs.rs`) makes one `SetWcsOrigin` and runs it through `history.execute`. The UI does no new world-level math. It only edits the draft angles, as before. The test asserts that `SetWcs` is queued.
- Pane text and the decision file now say "setup axes". Files are 275 and 242 lines. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` added. `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1495` are present. No snapshot, golden, dependency, `.github`, script or process-file change.

**Results (merged with main, which was already up to date at 4f4edcf; run locally, no runner was reachable)**
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (ui lib, boundary, boundary_picks, sinker_setup, theme_files, CWD `crates/ui`) | ok: 775 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (lib) and all four suites ok |
| Pin `quarter_turns_follow_each_oblique_setup_axis_in_both_directions` | ok |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test setup_wcs --test wcs_tilt --test turn_pivot` | ok: 7, 5, 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the mutation check myself. The hand check of the three rotation formulas above gives the same confidence.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Stale comment: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs:325` says `turn_model` uses the "`turn_wcs` law (the turn premultiplies ...)". After this PR, `turn_wcs` post-multiplies. The Model page still turns about WORLD axes on purpose (its label and `docs/user-guide/vendor-fixtures.md:26` say so), so the behavior is right. Only the comment is wrong. Also `wcs_page_tests.rs:151` says "about the world X" for a test that starts from a frame with no rotation, where both readings give the same result.
2. Missing test coverage, for a later follow-up (`P7`): (a) no test turns several times in a row. The math is right (each turn is again a right product on the new orientation), and the PR comment reports scratch probes at gimbal lock, but nothing in the tree pins it. (b) The PR adds no undo/redo test for a turn. Undo of `SetWcsOrigin` is covered in `crates/app/tests/commands_undo.rs:293`, and `turn_wcs` adds no new command, so I judge this enough. (c) No app-level test generates and posts a job after a turn. An X or Y turn gives a tilted frame, and `crates/app/tests/wcs_tilt.rs` already pins that generation refuses a tilted frame by name. Z turns are covered by `wcs_tilt.rs:78`. Posted coordinates after a Z turn depend only on the stored `Location`, which the new test checks.
3. `turn_wcs` reads the roll, pitch and yaw drafts, not the world. This was true before the PR. The drafts are synced from the world (`sync_setup_ui`), so the turn is applied to what the pane shows. Not a change in behavior.
4. Overlap with open PR #1209 (WCS page footer): #1209 does not touch `wcs_page.rs`, `wcs_page_tests.rs` or `turn_wcs`. Its files are `wcs_footer.rs`, `pages.rs` (the `wcs_page` call site), `mod.rs`, `tests.rs`, `tests/one_wcs.rs` and others. It also changes `pages.rs`, but in `wcs_page`, not near line 325. I expect no textual conflict. Its decision file says #759 (the split into `wcs_page.rs`) was meant to land first, and that has happened.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
